payload.task_text:
I work in the academic office and we want to review the grade distributions for our Spring 2014 courses and also collect student feedback through a survey.

First, please look up all courses from Spring 2014 in our learning management system. For each course, I need to analyze the assignment submissions to compute grade statistics: the average score, the median score, the pass rate (percentage of submissions with score >= 60), and the total number of distinct students who submitted graded work (count each student once).

Create an Excel file called "Grade_Distribution_Report.xlsx" in the workspace with two sheets. The first sheet called "Course Grades" should have columns Course_Code, Course_Name, Avg_Grade, Median_Grade, Pass_Rate, and Total_Students. Include one row per Spring 2014 course. The second sheet called "Summary" should have columns Metric and Value with rows for Total_Courses (number of Spring 2014 courses), Overall_Avg_Grade (average across all courses), Highest_Avg_Course (name of course with highest average grade), and Lowest_Avg_Course (name of course with lowest average grade). Write all computed numbers as plain numeric values (do not write Excel formulas), and use the course code and full course name as they appear in the learning management system.

Second, create a survey form titled "Spring 2014 Course Feedback Survey" to collect student opinions. The form should have at least 4 questions: overall satisfaction with the course (as a choice question with options Excellent, Good, Fair, Poor), teaching quality rating (as a choice question with options 1 through 5), how they found the workload (as a choice question with options Too Light, Manageable, Heavy, Overwhelming), and an open-ended suggestions question (as a text question, not required).

Finally, send an email from registrar@university.edu to students@university.edu with the subject "Spring 2014 Course Feedback Survey" informing students about the survey and encouraging them to participate.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, keep the large submission reads outside the main context with exactly one parallel collector wave, and let the main agent itself produce the workbook, the form and the email — no second wave.

The main agent resolves the accessible task workspace, calls canvas_list_courses(include_ended=true) once, and retains exactly the six Spring 2014 courses by full name/code (expected course_ids 6, 8, 12, 15, 19, 22). Validate unique course IDs, then dispatch one explore collector per course.

Wave 1 — dispatch exactly 6 explore sub-agents in parallel, one per literal Spring course. Every collector follows the same literal recipe with only its course substituted:

1. explore 0 (enterprise-data-analyst 0): Collector for course_id=6 (course_code and course_name as listed). A strictly read-only Canvas collector: call canvas_list_student_submissions(course_id=6, per_page=100, page=1), then keep calling page=2,3,... while pagination.has_more is true. The tool result may be truncated in the chat preview — always read the FULL JSON from the output_path file given in the result. A submission counts as graded iff it has a non-null numeric score field and workflow_state == "graded". Scores are on a 0-100 percentage scale. Aggregate all graded submissions in one script execution and return ONLY the compact JSON {course_id:6, course_code, course_name, avg_score, median_score, pass_rate, total_students, graded_count, pages}, where avg_score/median_score are the mean/median of graded scores, pass_rate = 100 * count(score >= 60) / graded_count, and total_students = number of DISTINCT user_ids among graded submissions. Do not return the row set, write any workspace file, or modify Canvas.
2. explore 1 (enterprise-data-analyst 1): Collector for course_id=8 — same literal recipe, only the course substituted.
3. explore 2 (enterprise-data-analyst 2): Collector for course_id=12 — same literal recipe, only the course substituted.
4. explore 3 (enterprise-data-analyst 3): Collector for course_id=15 — same literal recipe, only the course substituted.
5. explore 4 (enterprise-data-analyst 4): Collector for course_id=19 — same literal recipe, only the course substituted.
6. explore 5 (enterprise-data-analyst 5): Collector for course_id=22 — same literal recipe, only the course substituted.

After Wave 1, verify all six handoffs in one single pass (never per-course iteration): exactly one handoff per course, non-null statistics, graded_count > 0. Compute the four Summary metrics from the six unrounded course averages: Overall_Avg_Grade as the equal-weight arithmetic mean of the six course averages (not a submission-weighted global average); Highest_Avg_Course / Lowest_Avg_Course by unrounded course averages with course_code ascending only as a tie-break; Total_Courses = 6.

The main agent then completes every output directly, with no further delegation: (a) build Grade_Distribution_Report.xlsx in the resolved workspace with exactly two sheets — "Course Grades" with header Course_Code, Course_Name, Avg_Grade, Median_Grade, Pass_Rate, Total_Students and one row per course, and "Summary" with header Metric, Value and the four metric rows — all values plain numbers (no Excel formulas), then read both populated ranges back; (b) call create_form(title="Spring 2014 Course Feedback Survey") exactly once, add the four required questions sequentially with exact types/options/required flags (satisfaction choice Excellent/Good/Fair/Poor; teaching-quality choice 1-5; workload choice Too Light/Manageable/Heavy/Overwhelming; open-ended optional text suggestions), and verify with get_form(formId); (c) search Sent mail for From registrar@university.edu, To students@university.edu, subject Spring 2014 Course Feedback Survey, send exactly once only if no exact match exists, and read the retained message back. Finally run ONE reconciliation turn covering the workbook read-back, the form ID and the sent message, then call claim_done. Do not dispatch any agent after Wave 1, do not add a verification wave, and do not expose raw submission rows to the main context.

nodes.text:
You are helping analyze grade data from a Canvas LMS instance. Your single task: fetch EVERY page of student submissions for Canvas course_id 6 and report the on-disk paths where each page's full JSON was saved.

KNOWN FACTS (verified already — do not re-verify):
- The tool mcp__canvas__canvas_list_student_submissions(course_id=6, student_ids=["all"], per_page=100, page=N, grouped=false) returns submissions for the whole course. Its JSON ends with a "pagination" block: {page, per_page, total_count, total_pages, has_more}.
- Each page's output is larger than the harness's 50000-character display limit, so the tool result you see will start with "Tool output exceeded 50000 characters; showing a preview only." and will include an "output_path:" line pointing to the full JSON file on disk. This is EXPECTED. The complete data is safely stored at that output_path; you only see a preview.

YOUR STEPS:
1. Call canvas_list_student_submissions with course_id=6, per_page=100, page=1. From the result metadata extract: output_path, total_count, total_pages.
2. Loop: call the same tool for page=2, 3, ... up to total_pages (you may stop early if a response says has_more=false). For EVERY call, record the output_path line exactly as shown. Keep going until you have fetched all total_pages pages. Course 6 may need dozens of pages (possibly 40-130). Do not stop early; completeness is the only acceptance criterion.
3. If a page call errors or times out, retry it up to 3 times before reporting failure.
4. Do NOT read the output files, do NOT parse submission contents, do NOT compute any statistics. Your job is purely to page through the data and collect the output_path strings.

RETURN (final message), exactly this report:
- course_id: 6
- total_count: <from page 1 pagination>
- total_pages: <from page 1 pagination>
- pages_fetched: <count>
- failed_pages: <list, or "none">
- output_paths: <one file path per line, in page order, complete and unmodified>
Fetch all submissions for 6 Spring 2014 Canvas courses
